findings.evidence: Scope lock: "Three deliverables: two pure functions ... plus one explicitly impure function, `loadGatePolicy(repoRoot)`, which reads `<repoRoot>/afk.config.json` and delegates to the validator. All three ship with a success-path assertion." Manifest B-08 then: "the first returns the policy deep-equal to what was written", observed by "asserts all four outcomes, so an implementation that always returns null fails case one"; manifest B-12 when: "loadGatePolicy(repoRoot) is called".
findings.expected: Every export in the pinned surface is covered by the scope lock and has a declared observable for its primary success path, so the slice cannot ship green with that export broken.
findings.observed: loadGatePolicy is now named in the scope lock as the third, explicitly impure deliverable, and its read-and-parse success path is asserted twice: B-08 case one over a mkdtempSync config carrying a well-formed gatePolicy, and B-12 over this repository's committed afk.config.json. The definition of done also requires a passing assertion for loadGatePolicy's success path. An always-null implementation fails B-08 and B-12.
findings.clearCondition: Either drop loadGatePolicy from the pinned surface, or name it in the scope lock as an explicitly impure deliverable with a declared success-path assertion (loadGatePolicy over a directory that does contain a gatePolicy-bearing afk.config.json).

findings.evidence: Manifest B-01: given "src/gate-policy.ts imported as a namespace", when "Object.keys of that namespace is sorted", observed by "asserts the sorted keys deep-equal that six-name list, so an extra or missing runtime export fails".
findings.expected: The contract's "exports the surface pinned above and no other runtime value" clause, repeated in the definition of done, needs an observable that can fail when the surface is wrong.
findings.observed: B-01 no longer leans on typecheck alone for the exactness claim: the observable enumerates the module's runtime exports and compares them against the six pinned names, so an extra export fails the tests gate while typecheck keeps pinning the signatures.
findings.clearCondition: B-01's observable names an assertion that enumerates the module's exports, or the "exactly" wording is softened to the set the declared evidence actually pins.

findings.evidence: P-01 observable: "asserts declarations.map(d => d.id) equals [typecheck, lint, tests] and the no-config load is null; pnpm run typecheck still accepts src/base-gates.ts"; P-02 observable: "asserts those three values and that the sorted top-level keys equal [architectureDoc, gatePolicy, resourceKeys, version]"; P-03 observable: "asserts the source has no acceptance-manifest import and no toLowerCase".
findings.expected: Each clause of an observable result is producible by one of the gates the behavior lists — here typecheck (pnpm run typecheck) and tests (pnpm run test).
findings.observed: Every remaining static clause now names the assertion in src/gate-policy.test.ts that produces it: resolveBaseGateDeclarations ids for P-01 (verified producible — src/base-gates.ts:16-24 maps BASE_GATE_IDS to declarations regardless of whether the sanity plan resolves a step, so the ids hold on an empty temp directory), readFileSync + JSON.parse over the committed config for P-02, and a readFileSync source scan for P-03. The byte-identity claim moved to the definition of done.
findings.clearCondition: Each static clause either names the assertion in src/gate-policy.test.ts that produces it, or is dropped from the observable and left to the definition of done.

findings.evidence: Manifest B-11 given: "one glob per rejected metacharacter of the enumerated set — src/?.ts, src/[ab].ts, src/a].ts, src/{a,b}.ts, src/a}.ts, src/(a).ts, src/a).ts, src/!a.ts, src/a+.ts, src/a@.ts, src\\a.ts — plus src/***.ts and a**/b.ts"; observed by "the backslash case pins the pair against B-09, where a backslash in a path is normalized".
findings.expected: The observable covers the rejection set the behavior enumerates, or the behavior states that the listed values are representative.
findings.observed: The given now carries one glob per character of the contract's enumerated set `? [ ] { } ( ) ! + @ \`, backslash included, plus the two malformed-star segments; and the backslash glob is deliberately paired with B-09's backslash-bearing path, pinning the reject-in-glob / normalize-in-path split that D6 leaves implicit.
findings.clearCondition: B-11's given either covers the full enumerated set (a backslash-bearing glob included) or says the values are a representative sample of one shared validator.

findings.evidence: Contract B-03: "A policy omitting `protectedPaths`, `riskClasses`, or either member of `protectedPaths` parses and returns the documented baselines", against manifest B-03's given: "four reduced policies: {version:1}, one without protectedPaths, one without riskClasses, one whose protectedPaths omits testGlobs".
findings.expected: Both halves of the "either member of protectedPaths" clause have a declared case, since prd.md D1 says "Both members are optional; each defaults to the values shown".
findings.observed: Only the testGlobs-omitted half is declared. No case supplies a protectedPaths object that carries testGlobs but omits gatePolicyPaths, so an implementation that defaults gatePolicyPaths only when the whole protectedPaths object is absent — and throws when it is present without that member — passes every declared observable while violating B-03's own text. B-05's rejection of the unknown member testGlob makes a partial protectedPaths object a realistic hand-edit.
findings.clearCondition: B-03's given adds a fifth policy whose protectedPaths supplies testGlobs and omits gatePolicyPaths, with the result deep-equal to the baseline-filled policy; or B-03's wording narrows to the single member the declared cases cover.

findings.evidence: Non-goals: "An `ARCHITECTURE.md` row; no check requires one and that file is shared." Against prd.md:526-527's ownership table, whose `ARCHITECTURE.md` row reads "own rows" in every slice column including 01, and prd.md D6: "Accepted cost: the dialect is AFK's own and must be documented, not inherited."
findings.expected: A non-goal that overrides a parent-PRD ownership row says so and names where the deferred obligation lands, so the glob dialect's documentation is not lost between slices.
findings.observed: The "no check requires one" half checks out — no gate or test in this repository asserts ARCHITECTURE.md module coverage (the only src reader of architectureDoc is src/context-envelope.ts, which ships the file's contents into the envelope), so nothing goes red and the lock stays reliable. But the non-goal contradicts prd.md's file map without citing it, and D6's documentation obligation for AFK's own dialect is left with no owner named.
findings.clearCondition: The non-goal cites prd.md:527's "own rows" and names who documents the dialect instead (a later slice, or a follow-up), or ARCHITECTURE.md joins the file scope with a behavior pinning the added row.
